sans.$description: Everything on screen: display, sentence, UI, prose. One family across weights rather than two neutral Korean sans-serifs paired against each other — the S2 audit found IBM Plex Sans KR + Pretendard to be the similar-but-not-identical pairing that reads as indecision. Its Latin is IBM Plex Sans, so Latin and Hangul are matched by construction rather than by luck, which is what the Korean gate actually asks for.

mono.$description: The blank notation, figures and meta. Same superfamily as the sans, so the difference between them is register and not brand. Nanum Gothic Coding is not a fallback of convenience — IBM Plex Mono has no Hangul, and this is one of very few Korean monospace faces with a real bold.

serif.$description: Sustained reading, and the whole of the ebook interior. This is the real contrast axis in the system — serif against sans, not sans against sans. It is also where the print half gets its own voice, which the S2 lock requires, since the interior argues by being written on rather than by depicting the chain.
